publisher: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (with Census Bureau fieldwork)
survey_name: American Time Use Survey (ATUS)
edition_reference_period: 2025 annual averages; news release USDL-26-1022 published 2026-06-25
collection_period: Continuous, daily interviews Jan-Dec 2025; suspended 2025-10-01 to 2025-11-12 (federal shutdown), diaries for 2025-09-30 to 2025-11-11 missing; resumed 2025-11-13
slot_length: n/a (event-based diary; activities recorded with start/stop times, no fixed slots)
activity_classification: ATUS Coding Lexicon (6-digit codes, 17 major categories)
caveats: Shutdown gap Oct-mid Nov 2025: BLS re-weighted Nov 12-Dec 30 diaries to represent whole Q4 and says effect cannot be quantified. Table A-3 time-of-day is all-days annual average only (no weekday/weekend or age split published); derivation by weekday/weekend/age needs microdata. Diary day is 4:00 to 4:00 (hour 4 AM starts a new diary day). Secondary activities not collected except childcare of children under 13. Weekend days oversampled in design (weighted 5/7 weekday, 2/7 weekend). Interviews about 6,100 persons in 2025 (Technical Note). Universe is civilian noninstitutional population 15+. Public-use microdata listed as a separate register row by the subagent was folded into this row at merge (see timeuse_harmonisation microdata_access).

survey_name: NTIA Internet Use Survey (CPS Computer and Internet Use Supplement)
edition_reference_period: November 2023 (17th edition; datasets released 2024-08-30 per download page); NTIA Data Explorer and ntia-analyze-table.csv
age_floor: 3 (household questions persons 3+; online-activity questions asked of one randomly selected internet user aged 15+ per household)
caveats: Asks "watch videos over the Internet (examples YouTube and Netflix)" (PEVIDEO), which is on-demand plus live video without a live-stream item; no live-stream question found in the questionnaire, no language variable. Activity items answered by one randomly selected internet user aged 15+ per household; proxy responses allowed in the CPS supplement generally. Age bands in ntia-analyze-table.csv: 3-14, 15-24, 25-44, 45-64, 65+. A 2025 edition was planned for the November 2025 CPS (NTIA notice seeking OMB approval; 2025 draft questionnaire has the same online video item and no live-stream item) but no 2025 dataset is posted on the NTIA download page as of 2026-09-30; whether fieldwork was completed after the Oct-Nov 2025 shutdown is unverified. Questionnaire retrieved was the Draft for Public Comment / Final Draft for OMB Review; wording cross-checked against Nov 2023 technical documentation. Table figures come from ntia-analyze-table.csv (summary tabulations, not microdata). Raw CSV saved in raw/.

survey_name: Americans' Social Media Use 2025 (National Public Opinion Reference Survey, NPORS 2025)
caveats: Address-based sample, multimode (web, mail, phone), n=5,022 adults. Measures ever using YouTube etc., not live streaming. YouTube is the only video-oriented item; no Twitch or live-stream item found in the report (grep of report PDF) . Age bands 18-29, 30-49, 50-64, 65+.

survey_name: Teens, Social Media and AI Chatbots 2025
caveats: KnowledgePanel is a probability-based web panel; n=1,458 teens. Ever use YouTube; no live-stream item. Universe excludes teens not living with parents.

survey_name: American Trends Panel Wave 168 (streaming services items, short read 2025-07-01)
caveats: ATP recruited by address-based sampling; n=9,397. Streaming of TV/film subscription services (Netflix, Disney+, Prime Video); not live streams.

survey_name: American Community Survey 1-year estimates (tables B16004, S1601)
edition_reference_period: 2024 ACS 1-year (latest 1-year available on data.census.gov API; release month not verified; 2025 1-year release date not yet announced as of 2026-09-30)
age_floor: 5 (language questions asked of persons 5+; universe population 5 years and over)
caveats: Self-reported English ability; age bands in B16004/S1601 tables only 5-17, 18-64, 65+; finer age needs ACS PUMS (later stage). Language spoken at home asked only about languages other than English (no English proficiency for English-only households, who are counted as English speakers). Retrieved via data.census.gov table API (api.census.gov requires key). Figures are estimates with margins of error (MOE in raw JSON). Population includes household and group quarters. 2025 1-year not released; 2020-2024 5-year released 2026-01-29 (not used).

survey_name: How Hispanic Americans Get Their News (2023 survey of Hispanic adults; ATP wave 138 and KnowledgePanel)
caveats: Only I4-type item found for the US: language in which Hispanic adults get news (mostly English / mostly Spanish / both equally). Universe is Hispanic adults only (n=5,078: 1,524 ATP plus 3,554 KnowledgePanel), all news media, not online video. Both panels recruited by random address-based sampling.

survey_name: Time Use Survey 2022 (General Social Survey Time Use cycle); tables 45-10-0104-01, 45-10-0105-01; visualization tool 71-607-X2025002; PUMF 45-25-0001 (2022)
collection_period: 2022-07-16 to 2023-07-15 (one year, reference day assigned so days of week balanced)
activity_classification: Time Use Survey activity coding; published groups: sleep, personal care, eating, transportation, paid work/studying or learning, unpaid care, unpaid domestic work, socializing, active leisure, passive leisure, other
caveats: Time-of-day table 45-10-0105-01 (main activity only): participation rate by 5-minute interval, weekdays / weekends / all days, age 15-34, 35-54, 55-64, 65+, men+/women+, Canada only (no provinces); paid work and studying are one combined group; passive leisure includes watching TV or videos, reading, listening to music/radio/podcasts (note 12) so online video is not separable from TV; active leisure includes "use of technology". Excludes Territories and institutionalized and residents of First Nations reserves. Approx 45,000 dwellings sampled, response rate 30.7% (IMDB). Survey collects simultaneous activity in the diary but published tables and tempograms use main activity only. PUMF released under Statistics Canada Open Licence (zip with CSV and documentation), not downloaded (later stage). Collection not COVID-fieldwork-era in the 2020-21 sense but some post-pandemic behaviour (telework) reflected. Table CSVs saved in raw/. Diary day 04:00 to 04:00 confirmed at https://www.statcan.gc.ca/en/survey/household/4503/diary-instructions. Secondary activity: simultaneous-activity question in diary; published multitasking estimates found only in Telework, time use and well-being (89-652-X2024003). Time-of-day table 45-10-0105-01: about half of age-band participation cells are published as '..' (not available), more on weekends; totals and sex splits are near complete. Public-use microdata listed as a separate register row by the subagent was folded into this row at merge (see timeuse_harmonisation microdata_access).

survey_name: Canadian Internet Use Survey (CIUS) 2022; tables 22-10-0136-01 and 22-10-0137-01; Insights/presentation 11-631-X2025002; article 75-006-X2025001-00007
edition_reference_period: 2022 cycle (results released 2023-07-20; a CIUS PUMF is announced in a The Daily item titled "Data availability for Canadian Internet Use Survey: Public use microdata file" (2024-04-16, seen in search results only, not fetched)); tables also carry 2018 and 2020 cycles
caveats: Only official source found with a live-stream item: UI_Q040B "Watched live-streaming services, excluding user-generated content" (past 3 months), plus separate items for user-generated video (YouTube, Twitch, TikTok) and eSports/video game streaming. The 2022 live-stream item is published by age only for 15-24 and total (11-631-X2025002), not in tables 22-10-0136/0137; the 2020 cycle (fieldwork Nov 2020 to Mar 2021, COVID era) has age bands 15-24/25-44/45-64/65+ for streamed or live-streamed sports, live TV, eSports, other video gaming services in table 22-10-0137-01. Two-stage stratified probability sample, about 55,700 sample units, response rate 45.3% (IMDB); mail and phone invitations. Tables state values as percentage of Canadians 15+ (note 4), non-internet-users counted as not doing the activity; some StatCan articles report shares among internet users instead (e.g. 72% UGV in The Daily 2025-05-21). Content-origin items UI_Q041A-D (English-language / French-language Canadian content / foreign) exist in questionnaire but no published table found. 2022 CIUS PUMF exists (Borealis, open licence per search listing; not verified further, not downloaded). Microdata: CIUS 2022 PUMF announced (not verified). Tier set to 2 at merge (official ICT household survey).

survey_name: Canadian Internet Use Survey (CIUS) 2020 (older edition, used only for age-banded live-stream-type items missing for 2022 in tables)
caveats: COVID-era fieldwork (Nov 2020 to Mar 2021); superseded by CA-STATCAN-CIUS-2022; recorded only because the 22-10-0137-01 table has no 2022 values for live-stream sports, eSports and other live/streamed TV by age. Fieldwork dates from The Daily 2021-06-22. Tier set to 2 at merge (official ICT household survey, not a time-use diary). COVID-era fieldwork Nov 2020 to Mar 2021.

survey_name: Census of Population 2021, knowledge of official languages by age (table 98-10-0225-01; 100% data)
collection_period: 2021 Census collection (spring 2021, during COVID-19; exact dates not verified in this session)
age_floor: 0 (all persons; question asked of entire population)
caveats: Self-reported "Can this person speak English or French well enough to conduct a conversation?" (no graded proficiency scale; conversation threshold). Category "English only" and "English and French" both imply English ability; French-only excludes English. Universe: all persons excluding institutional residents; excludes data for incompletely enumerated reserves. 2021 Census conducted during COVID-19; next census is 2026 (results not yet released as of 2026-09-30, not checked). First official language spoken and mother tongue by age in other 98-10 tables not recorded.

publisher: CRTC (data from Media Technology Monitor, MTM)
survey_name: CRTC Communications Market Report: Annual highlights of the broadcasting sector 2024-2025 (MTM Fall 2025 survey of Canadians 18+)
collection_period: Fall 2025 (MTM fall survey; exact dates not stated in text fetched)
caveats: MTM is an industry-run survey (mtm-otm.ca) reported by the regulator; telephone interviews with a regionally representative sample of landline and cell-only Canadians; fall 2025 n=8,370 adults (4,570 Anglophones, 3,800 Francophones); respondents self-identify as Anglophone/Francophone. Weighting and response rate not stated in text fetched. Measures subscriptions to online audiovisual services and audio streaming, not live-stream viewing; no language-of-content item found. crtc.gc.ca returns 403 to WebFetch and curl; read via Parallel web_fetch excerpts (chart data tables not retrievable). Other data in the report come from Numeris (commercial) and Vividata (commercial online panel) and are not recorded.

publisher: Office for National Statistics (ONS); fieldwork NatCen Opinion Panel
survey_name: Time use in the UK (Online Time Use Survey, OTUS; ONS Time Use Study), dataset edition March 2024
edition_reference_period: Wave 9 to 17 March 2024 (dataset also holds 8 waves 28 Mar 2020 to 9-17 Mar 2024)
collection_period: 2020-03-28 to 2024-03-17 in 8 one-week to six-week waves; latest wave 9-17 March 2024
activity_classification: ONS OTUS activity categorisation (aggregated categories; see Activity_categorisation sheet)
caveats: Official statistics in development (previously labelled experimental). Published estimates use MAIN activities only; secondary or passive activities excluded (Cover_sheet). Daily-mean minutes and participation shares only; no time-of-day tables in dataset (worksheets 1-25 checked). Single-week wave (9-17 Mar 2024) so not full-year coverage. Sample drawn from NatCen Opinion Panel (probability-recruited from BSA / Scottish SA / Life in NI / Consumer Protection Study); sept 2023 wave response 36.6% of diaries. Two diary days per person (one weekday, one weekend day; weekday:weekend rescaled 5:2). Waves 2020-2021 in same dataset are COVID-era and GB-only (18+, GB), from 2022 UK. Ad hoc table 2097 (weekday vs weekend, March 2024, n=3,477 diaries) published 24 May 2024. Lead said 'Spring 2024 tables via ESCoE/NatCen': the ONS/ESCoE Time Use Study run by NatCen is the same OTUS series; the tables are the ONS March 2024 release, not a separate ESCoE dataset.

survey_name: Time use in the UK: 23 September to 1 October 2023 (OTUS bulletin and dataset)
caveats: SUPERSEDED by March 2024 dataset edition (UK-ONS-OTUS-2024MAR); this is the latest BULLETIN (released 9 Nov 2023) but no later bulletin exists. Experimental statistics. 5,000 adults sampled, 10,000 diary days issued, 3,659 (36.6%) diaries completed and weighted. Main activities only in estimates. No time-of-day tables. No figures recorded from this edition (all present in the later edition).

publisher: Office for National Statistics; distributed by UK Data Service
survey_name: Online Time Use Survey, 2020-2024: Secure Access (UKDS SN 9204, DOI 10.5255/UKDA-SN-9204-3)
edition_reference_period: 2020-2024, 3rd edition released May 2026 (file last updated 19 May 2026)
caveats: Microdata; Secure Access only (per project owner; UKDS catalogue page is JavaScript-rendered and could not be read, only the title/edition page was fetched). Variable list (secondary activity, location, English ability) NOT verified. OTUS diaries record up to five secondary activities per slot in the instrument (ONS bulletin), so secondary-activity microdata plausibly present: unverified. Microdata not downloaded (stage 3+).

publisher: Centre for Time Use Research (UCL) with NatCen Opinion Panel; ESRC funded; UK Data Service SN 9336
survey_name: Centre for Time Use Research UK Time Use Survey, March 2023 (ELiDDI online diary)
slot_length: not found (HETUS-compatible activity and diary fields per catalogue snippet; slot length not stated in NatCen technical info)
caveats: Academic (CTUR/UCL) study fielded by NatCen Opinion Panel (random-probability recruited via BSA and NI Consumer Protection Study); 2,174 panellists completed >=1 diary, 3,779 days, day-level response 35%; main and secondary activities, location, enjoyment, device use captured (NatCen technical info, fetched). Microdata only, no published tables found. Single month, not full-year. Access level from UKDS: registration assumed (UKDS catalogue page JS-rendered; not verified).

publisher: Centre for Time Use Research (Oxford) commissioned; fieldwork NatCen; ESRC; UK Data Service SN 8128
survey_name: United Kingdom Time Use Survey, 2014-2015 (UKTUS; UK Time Diary Study; UK contribution to HETUS)
collection_period: 2014-03-31 to 2015-05-18 (fieldwork dates per NatCen technical report; report also states April 2014 to December 2015)
activity_classification: HETUS-style UKTUS activity coding list (NatCen appendix)
caveats: OLDER EDITION recorded because the latest ONS OTUS has no time-of-day tables and microdata are Secure Access only; UKTUS microdata (10-minute slots, primary+secondary activity, location) allow derivation of a time-of-day profile. Multi-stage stratified probability sample of addresses (PAF; NI wards); household response 40.4%; all household members aged 8+ diaried (two days: one weekday, one weekend day); 4,741 households per CTUR page; England, Scotland, Wales, NI. Pre-COVID (2014-15) so may be out of date on working-from-home and streaming. No published time-of-day tables found on UKDS/CTUR pages fetched. Access: UKDS End User Licence; download after registration (not verified in browser).

survey_name: Online Nation 2025 report
caveats: Report PDF read via Parallel web_fetch excerpts (ofcom.org.uk blocks curl and WebFetch). Adult data come from the Online Experiences Tracker (online panel, 7,000+ internet users), the YouGov-based Online Research Panel and Ipsos iris passive measurement (18+ internet users): non-probability. No adult live-stream viewing share found; children 8-17 item on seeing harmful content while watching a live stream (12%) is not the measure and was not recorded. Tier pending (regulator, opt-in panels).

survey_name: Media Nations 2026 (UK)
caveats: NOT FETCHED (Cloudflare 403, see UK-OFCOM-ONLINENATION-2025). Exists per search snippets only. Combines BARB, Ofcom and industry data; audience measurement basis unverified. Not fetched in merge step either.

publisher: Office for National Statistics (Opinions and Lifestyle Survey)
survey_name: Internet access - households and individuals, Great Britain: 2020
caveats: DISCONTINUED: ONS notice dated 3 May 2023 says the release is discontinued and points to the Ofcom Technology Tracker. Great Britain only. Opinions and Lifestyle Survey (mixed-mode from 2020). Fieldwork Jan-Feb 2020 (pre-lockdown). No live-stream or online-video-by-age figure extracted (bulletin text fetched does not mention video streaming). Sample design and age floor not stated on the fetched page.

publisher: RAJAR (Radio Joint Audience Research Ltd; contractor Ipsos UK; RSMB)
survey_name: RAJAR quarterly data release Q2 2026 (radio listening by location)
slot_length: 15 (quarter-hour diary slots per search snippet; not verified on page fetched)
caveats: Industry-body survey. Methodology overview (fetched): hybrid of 15,000 quarterly face-to-face-recruited 7-day diaries (paper/online/mobile), a 5,000 passive app-based MediaCell panel and ~1,000 diary boost panel; over 22,000 adults 15+ per quarter, contractor Ipsos UK. Probability status of the recruitment is not stated on the page. Listening by location (in home, in vehicle, work/elsewhere) published quarterly; 'work/elsewhere' is a combined category so at-work listening is not isolated. Radio only (no podcasts/video). Infographic text says 12% but chart label shows 13% for work/elsewhere share: recorded as text.

survey_name: Census 2021 England and Wales: TS029 Proficiency in English; RM111 Proficiency in English by age
edition_reference_period: Census Day 21 March 2021 (TS029 v1 released 29 Nov 2022, superseded versions 30 Jan 2023 and 28 Mar 2023; RM111 released 28 Mar 2023)
collection_period: 2021-03-21 (census day; collected online and paper Mar-Apr 2021)
caveats: COVID-era census (Census Day 21 March 2021, national lockdown). Self-reported proficiency asked only of people whose main language is not English (English or Welsh in Wales). Universe usual residents aged 3+. Data pulled from Nomis API (NM_2211_1 RM111 and NM_2048_1 TS029, England and Wales geography 2092957703) which serves the same ONS release. RM111 age bands are coarse (15 and under, 16-24, 25-34, 35-49, 50-64, 65+); proficiency categories in RM111 collapse very well/well and not well/not at all. Statistical disclosure control applied (record swapping, cell perturbation).

survey_name: Scotland's Census 2022: UV210 English language skills; UV210b by age (6 categories)
edition_reference_period: Census Day 20 March 2022; published 21 May 2024 (ethnic group, national identity, language and religion)
caveats: English skills asked of everyone aged 3+ on four skills (understand, speak, read, write) each on a 4-point scale; ten derived categories. UV210 (all ages) downloadable as output-area CSV from the UKDS CKAN S3 mirror (used here, national totals derived by summing OA rows); UV210b (by age, 6 categories) found but the UKDS CKAN pages return 403 and its CSV path could not be located, so by-age Scotland figures are 'exists, not accessible'. Scotland's Census site national report page fetched did not contain English skills numbers. Ten national totals the subagent summed from output-area rows were removed at merge (derived, not published); Scotland English skills remain a gap.

publisher: Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency
survey_name: Census 2021 Northern Ireland: MS-B14 Proficiency in English; DT-0034 English proficiency by age (11 categories) by sex
edition_reference_period: Census Day 21 March 2021; MS-B14 published 22 Sep 2022
caveats: COVID-era census. Proficiency asked only of people whose main language is not English; four-point scale (very well / well / not well / not at all). Age table pulled from NISRA Flexible Table Builder CSV (DT-0034 layout without sex). The 0-15 band includes 66,559 persons coded 'No code required' (under age 3, not asked).

survey_name: Information Society Statistics - Households (ICT Household Survey), 2025 edition
caveats: Headline indicators via Labour Force Survey instrument (14,635 respondents Q1+Q2 2025); detailed usage questions by online (CAWI) questionnaire with invitation letters to ~112,900 persons aged 16+, 4,034 respondents (survey background note, fetched). CSO 2024 questionnaire (fetched PDF) includes B3 items on internet streamed TV, VOD and video-sharing (e.g. YouTube) but no live-stream item, and the CSO PxStat publication pages found (ICA95/96/100) do not tabulate them: video-item figures for Ireland are taken from Eurostat isoc_ci_ac_i instead. The 2025 questionnaire round dropped the video items (Eurostat model). Age floor 16; upper age cap not verified.

survey_name: Census of Population 2022 Profile 5 (Diversity, Migration, Ethnicity, Irish Travellers & Religion): speakers of languages other than English or Irish at home by ability to speak English (PxStat F5015)
edition_reference_period: Census night 3 April 2022; Profile 5 released 26 Oct 2023
caveats: Ability to speak English is asked only of people who speak a language other than English or Irish at home (universe 751,507); so it is NOT a population-wide English-ability measure and no share of the total population is given. Scale very well / well / not well / not at all (plus not stated). F5015 breaks down by citizenship, not age; no age-by-English-ability table found among 5,253 PxStat tables updated since 26 Oct 2023 (F5029, F7117 and SAP2022T2T6ED also not by age).

publisher: Economic and Social Research Institute (ESRI) for the NDP Gender Equality Unit, Dept of Justice, Equality and Law Reform
survey_name: Time Use in Ireland 2005: Survey Report (Research Series 183, first national time-use survey)
collection_period: 2005 (pilot April 2005; main fieldwork limited to 8 weeks; exact dates not verified)
caveats: OLD (2005) and the only national time-use survey of Ireland: no later CSO survey found; not in Eurostat HETUS 2020 round (tus_20 empty for IE). Not produced by the national statistics office (research institute, commissioned by a government unit), hence tier pending. Two-stage clustered random sample from the Electoral Register; 1,089 individuals in 585 households; household response 58%. 'Light' diary: respondent ticks any of 26 pre-coded activities per 15-minute slot, multiple activities allowed (27% of slots have 3+); main activity derived by priority list. 4am-4am diary, one weekday and one weekend day. Published tables are daily means and daily participation shares by sex/age group; NO time-of-day tables in the report. Location item (home / away) captured. Microdata availability not verified.

survey_name: Time Use Survey 2024 (How Australians use their time, 2024)
edition_reference_period: 2024 (published 2025-12-17; supplementary tables incl. Table 14 time of day released 2026-08-05)
collection_period: 2024-07-22 to 2024-09-03 and 2024-09-16 to 2024-10-29 (Aug-Oct 2024 per ABS headline; partial-year, late winter to spring only)
activity_classification: ABS Time Use Survey Activity Classification 2024 (4-digit; updated from 2020-21; Data Item List)
caveats: Online (CAWI) diary with activity picklist, 2 consecutive days, midnight-to-midnight, main activity only; secondary activity only for supervisory care of children/adults; location and who-with dropped (ABS methodology). Fieldwork 3 months only (Aug-Oct 2024), no full seasonal coverage. Sample 6,899 households, 10,613 persons, 19,319 diary days. Not comparable with 2020-21. Published time-of-day table is paid work only (Table 14); other activities by time of day only via DataLab microdata (approved users; time interval file has 288 5-min records/day, publishable at 5/15/30/60 min; TableBuilder not available). Published age bands only 15-24, 25-64, 65+ (plus 15-64). Diary: menu of activities, so under-reporting of activities not thought of as main (e.g. listening to music) noted by ABS. Table 14 time-of-day shares are of that day's paid-work participants (columns sum to 100), not of all persons.

survey_name: Time Use Survey 2020-21 (How Australians Use Their Time, 2020-21 financial year)
activity_classification: ABS Time Use Survey Activity Classification 2020-21 (Data Item List)
caveats: COVID-era collection: ABS says data for point-in-time analysis only and not comparable with previous or later years. Recorded although superseded because it is the only AU edition with secondary-activity, location and hourly time-of-day tables for sleep/work/domestic/childcare/free time (Tables 13-17). Secondary activity reported for only ~12% of waking time (ABS 2024 methodology). No microdata released (ABS microdata page), although the 2020-21 data item list contains language spoken at home, proficiency in spoken English and personal IT use.

survey_name: Census of Population and Housing 2021: Language used at home and Proficiency in Spoken English (General Community Profile G11, G13)
activity_classification: ASCL language classification; census variables LANP and ENGLP
caveats: GCP G13 (language x proficiency x sex) has no age split; G11 has age (0-14 ... 85+) but for overseas-born persons only. All-persons age x proficiency requires Census TableBuilder (free registration; not fetched). Proficiency is self-assessed, asked only of those using a language other than English at home; scale Very well / Well / Not well / Not at all (GCP merges into "Very well or well" and "Not well or not at all"). Non-response ENGLP 5.5%, LANP 5.7% (ABS dictionary). Census night 2021-08-10 during COVID-19 lockdowns in some states (enumeration, not a diary).

survey_name: Household Use of Information Technology, Australia
caveats: DISCONTINUED: ABS page states "This release has ceased" with no future releases. Recorded only to document the gap; no figures recorded (pre-live-stream era; only household internet access and general activity shares seen on release page).

publisher: Australian Communications and Media Authority (fieldwork by The Social Research Centre)
survey_name: Communications and media in Australia: How we watch and listen to content (ACMA annual consumer survey, Survey 1)
caveats: Probability-based online panel (Life in Australia, SRC) with phone follow-up for offline people; representative of adults 18+; weighted. Exec summary reports age bands 18-24, 25-34, 35-44, 45-54, 55-64, 65-74, 75+ only where differences are noted; full tables only in interactive report (export from the report; interactive page not retrievable: ACMA site returned 503/403 to direct fetch; content read via Parallel web_fetch of the PDF and methodology). No live-stream question found; closest are user-generated/short-form online video (e.g. YouTube, TikTok, Instagram), YouTube use, and Twitch (item in F7 list since 2022). Panel weighting details, response rates and per-item question stems not in fetched documents. Some 18-24 cells have small bases (n=525 in 2025).

publisher: Australian Communications and Media Authority (fieldwork by The Social Research Centre)
survey_name: Communications and media in Australia: How we watch and listen to content (ACMA annual consumer survey, Survey 1)
caveats: SUPERSEDED edition; recorded only because the 2024 executive summary text reports Twitch (closest live-streaming service) by sex and location while the 2025 summary does not. Same methodology as 2025.

survey_name: Time Use Survey 2009/10
activity_classification: ACTUS (New Zealand Activity Classification for the Time Use Survey; Aas four categories of time; not ICATUS)
caveats: Latest NZ time use survey found (1998/99 and 2009/10 only; 16 years old). Stats NZ 2018-22 household surveys programme (third edition) proposed a shortened time use supplement to the NZGSS from 2020 (12-yearly) but no resulting release was found. Two-day (48-hour) paper diary, primary plus simultaneous activity, location and who-with captured; 8,543 households selected, 9,159 respondents, household response 72%, personal cooperation 86%. First release included hourly proportion working by weekday/weekend (per user guide) but the archive.stats.govt.nz release pages are offline and the supplementary-tables page is JS-rendered, so no time-of-day figure was retrievable; unit records only via Stats NZ Data Lab. Diary-day start hour not stated in the user guide text read. Pre-dates smartphones/live streaming.

survey_name: 2023 Census: languages spoken
collection_period: 2023 Census (census night date not stated on fetched pages)
activity_classification: Stats NZ language classification (languages spoken, total responses; 17 categories in ADE tables)
caveats: Question asks which languages the person can have a conversation about a lot of everyday things in (up to six; includes NZ Sign Language); no graded proficiency scale. Language response 85.3% from 2023 forms, 8.8% from earlier censuses, 5.8% imputed (Figure.NZ table note quoting Stats NZ). Age x language tables exist in Aotearoa Data Explorer (e.g. CEN23_ECI_021 languages spoken x age 5-year groups x birthplace x gender, NZ total available) but the Data Explorer API requires a subscription key and pages are JS-rendered, so values by age were not retrieved. Only the total te reo Maori figure and rounded English figure were fetched.

survey_name: Household Use of Information and Communication Technology
caveats: DISCONTINUED/SUPERSEDED: last edition found; release page says 2015 edition would be published April 2016 but none was found. Supplement to the Household Labour Force Survey (persons 15+ in private dwellings). Copy of the Stats NZ release hosted by NZ Herald because archive.stats.govt.nz is offline. Excel tables not retrievable. Pre-dates live streaming.

survey_name: Where Are The Audiences? 2026 (WATA), incl. Youth sub-report
caveats: Commissioned survey by public funder: n=1,701 (online 1,251 + phone 450) with boosts for Maori, Pacific, Asian and 15-24; weighted to 2023 Census on age x gender, region, ethnicity and interview day. Sampling frame / recruitment (panel vs random) not stated in the report; margin of error stated for 2024 edition (+/-2.6%, n=1,408, Glasshouse Consulting). Measures media use "yesterday" incl. time-of-day windows; no live-stream, language-of-content or English-ability questions. Youth report (n=360 aged 15-24) at https://www.nzonair.govt.nz/documents/1416/Where_Are_The_Youth_Audiences_2026_Report.pdf. Edition prior to 2024 by Colmar Brunton; question wording changed across waves.

survey_name: Encuesta Nacional sobre Uso del Tiempo (ENUT) 2024
collection_period: 2024-10-07 to 2024-11-29 (8 weeks, Oct-Nov only); results published 2025-08-28
caveats: NOT A DIARY: stylised questionnaire (83 questions, 7 sections) asking yes/no and hours+minutes per pre-set activity for the previous week, with separate answers for weekdays (lunes a viernes) and weekend (sabado y domingo). No time-of-day information. Simultaneous activities are not recorded as such: interviewer instruction is to split time between activities done at the same time; only passive childcare (vigilar mientras hacia otra cosa) is captured as a secondary activity. Media use items are worded sin hacer otra actividad (as sole activity). Fieldwork 8 weeks in Oct-Nov (not full year; no seasonality). Sample 32048 dwellings (2000 in indigenous-language localities). Quinquennial (previous 2019, 2014). Tier 1 by brief definition (official time-use survey) but flagged: daily/weekly totals only, cannot yield half-hour availability profile. Tabulados not retrieved; figures taken from INEGI Reporte de resultados 29/25. Access detail: tabulados tab exists; open microdata download per INEGI microdata policy; neither file list retrievable in this session. Tier set to pending at merge: stylised weekly questionnaire, not a diary.

survey_name: Encuesta Nacional sobre Disponibilidad y Uso de Tecnologias de la Informacion en los Hogares (ENDUTIH) 2025
caveats: Latest edition (2024 edition published 2025-05-06 is superseded). Sample 65057 dwellings; reference population persons 6+ (121.9 million). Direct interview, individual respondent since 2015 redesign. Internet-use age bands: 6-14, 15-24, 25-34, 35-44, 45-54, 55-64, 65-74, 75+. No live-stream item found in published results; closest items are smartphone app use (acceder a contenidos de audio y video), internet use type (Entretenimiento, includes audiovisual content and reading) and household streaming service. No English-ability item (per secondary source Analisis Economico 2022; not verified on INEGI questionnaire). Streaming module added 2023. Access detail: tabulados and open-data CSV zip listed by INEGI; not downloaded: stage 3+.

publisher: Instituto Federal de Telecomunicaciones (IFT); regulator succeeded by Comision Reguladora de Telecomunicaciones (CRT) from 2025-10
survey_name: Encuesta Nacional de Consumo de Contenidos Audiovisuales (ENCCA) 2024
collection_period: 2024 (IFT press release states 2024 edition; fieldwork dates 2024-04-23 to 2024-06-03 appear only in secondary press summaries, not verified on publisher page)
caveats: Sample 8750 respondents (6125 urban, 2625 rural) per IFT communique; 1796 interviews with NNA aged 7-17; 4812 women. Sample design, adult age floor and weighting NOT verified because full adult report was not retrievable (somosaudiencias.ift.org.mx blocked; IFT website is now a historical archive; CRT is successor at gob.mx/crt). Regulator survey, probability design likely but unverified. Ninth consecutive annual-ish edition (2015-2024); no 2025/2026 edition found. Language/subtitle/dubbing items not visible in fetched material. Women-by-generation report cover is dated Marzo 2024 although fieldwork is 2024 (date inconsistency in publisher document). Access detail: full report on somosaudiencias.ift.org.mx unreachable via proxy in this session; only IFT press release, NNA report and women-by-generation report fetched.

survey_name: Modulo de Bienestar Autorreportado (BIARE) Ampliado 2014 (linked to MCS-ENIGH 2014)
caveats: Only INEGI instrument found that asks about English: item 8 Usted habla... 2. ingles (conversacion). Self-reported conversational ability, no proficiency scale. 2014, i.e. 12 years old, superseded/one-off; later BIARE editions not verified to contain the item. Access level for microdata not verified (INEGI microdata generally open); listed here as restricted=unknown. Published INEGI tables with English share not found; the only share found is a third-party computation from microdata.

survey_name: Censo de Poblacion y Vivienda 2020
caveats: Assessed for I2 only: the Censo 2020 Marco conceptual (fetched) covers indigenous-language questions; no English/foreign-language ability question found (English mentioned only in historical census notes). COVID-era enumeration (March 2020, curtailed). No figures recorded.

survey_name: EU survey on ICT usage in households and by individuals: internet activities (isoc_ci_ac_i)
edition_reference_period: Reference year 2024 (latest year carrying video items; dataset updated 2026-04-17); 2025 wave has no video items
caveats: Video items (I_IUVSS video sharing, I_IUSTV internet streamed TV live or catch-up, I_IUVOD, I_IUV) are asked only in even years: 2016,2018,2020,2022,2024; 2025 lacks them. No live-stream item, so all proxies. Iceland latest is 2020; Switzerland has no data. Universe 16-74; units PC_IND and PC_IND_IU3 both fetched. Model questionnaire 2024 item B3 j) and l) wording recorded in figures. Sampling generally stratified random, per-country national metadata. Also holds UK figures for reference year 2018 (last UK year in the dataset, pre-Brexit) and IE 2024; merged at stage 1 from two regional extracts.

survey_name: Omnibus 2025 (OMN2025): Erhebung zur Internetnutzung (PxWeb px-x-1604000000_102)
caveats: Only three age bands (15-29, 30-59, 60+). Items are films/videos and radio/TV over internet; exact questionnaire text not retrieved. About 3,000 respondents; two-yearly since 2017. Filled the Eurostat gap for CH.

survey_name: Adult Education Survey 2022: foreign language skills (edat_aes_l22, l32, l52)
caveats: No English-specific table. Language of the best-known foreign language is not identified. Self-reported scale (basic incl. very basic / good / proficient). Level tables are shares among people knowing at least one foreign language. Switzerland absent. Flags u (low reliability) and b (break) carried into notes. Age 18-69 since 2022; earlier waves 25-64.

survey_name: Strukturerhebung (Structural Survey) main languages, published in Sprachenlandschaft in der Schweiz 2022
caveats: First-language question only. ESRK 2019 language survey (15+, at least 10,000 persons, every five years) has finer language practice data; not located as table.

survey_name: Census of Population and Housing 2021 Final Report (language from early childhood)
caveats: nso.gov.mt returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) to every route tried, so no NSO table was read. Two figures quoted in news reports were removed at merge because they are not from the publisher. Status: exists, not accessible.

publisher: European Commission DG EAC / DG COMM (fieldwork Verian)
survey_name: Special Eurobarometer 540 Europeans and their languages (wave EB100.1)
caveats: Official Volume A (country) and Volume B (socio-demographic, EU27 only) xlsx tables downloaded from data.europa.eu (dataset s2979_100_1_sp540_eng); all country figures checked against Volume A at merge (135 values matched), EU27 age rows taken from Volume B. Fieldwork 2023-09-25 to 2023-10-19 (Volume A header). Face-to-face, about 1,000 per country (EU27 26,523), nationals of the 27 Member States only; no UK, NO, CH, IS. Commissioned survey: tier pending. English item counts English only as a non-mother-tongue language. Microdata at GESIS (ZA8778) contain language ability and internet use but no video item.

survey_name: Harmonised European time use surveys, 2020 round (tus_20)
activity_classification: HETUS ACL 2018 (aggregated to 41 categories; wide groups in startime table)
caveats: Only 11 countries loaded so far; 10 are in my group (BG DE EE HR HU NL AT PL FI NO). Fieldwork: EE 2019-2021, FI 2020-2021, AT 2021-2022, NL 2021-2023, DE 2022, BG HR NO 2022-2023, PL 2023, HU 2024-2025. COVID-era overlap for EE FI AT NL. Time-of-day table tus_20startime has sex split only (no age, no weekday/weekend). Secondary activity tables tus_20age2 (radio/recordings, TV, etc.), tus_20simuact, tus_20screen. Eurostat says further indicators in 2026 and other countries to follow; microdata not yet available.

survey_name: Harmonised European time use surveys, 2000 and 2010 waves (tus_00)
caveats: Used only for countries missing from tus_20: BE 2012-13, EL 2013-14, ES 2009-10, FR 2009-10, IT 2008-09, LU 2014-15, RO 2010-11 (wave 2010); LV 2003, LT 2003, SI 2000-01 (wave 2000). Old data. Microdata for 2010 wave via Eurostat research access. No HETUS data in Eurobase for CY CZ DK MT PT SK SE CH IS.

survey_name: Zeitverwendungserhebung (ZVE) 2022
caveats: Results page has an average-daily-schedule (Durchschnittlicher Tagesablauf) section and a weekday versus weekend leisure comparison; detailed tables in GENESIS; no dedicated secondary-activity table found on the results page. Earlier release of 2024-03 was corrected. About 10,000 households, 20,000 persons. Microdata via Forschungsdatenzentrum.

survey_name: Tidsbruksundersokelsen 2022 (statbank 14320-14324, 14339-14340)
activity_classification: national scheme (10-minute web diary; main and secondary activity, place, company)
caveats: Statbank tables fetched by API are daily averages (time spent, share performing) by activity incl. television viewing, gaming and social media, age 9-79 bands; no time-of-day statbank table located (SSB page says daily rhythm can be analysed). Time-of-day figures for Norway come from Eurostat tus_20startime. Gross sample 8,800.

survey_name: Tidsanvandningsundersokningen (TA) 2010/11
caveats: SCB page lists eight diagram sets by activity and life phase; no time-of-day tables or secondary activities seen; no further survey planned. Not in Eurobase.

survey_name: En fraga om tid (TID2021)
caveats: Activity-based questionnaire, not a diary: leisure not collected, activities do not sum to 24 hours, no time-of-day. Fielded during the pandemic. Cannot supply I5. Sample 18,000. Tier set to pending at merge: activity questionnaire, not a diary.

survey_name: Time use survey (experimental statistics)
caveats: Experimental. Web questionnaire logging two days, 5,000 sampled, 878 usable (17.7%). Two weeks of one November only, so not full year. Results one background variable at a time; age groups 18-29, 30-54, 70+ (as listed). No time-of-day tables.

survey_name: Indagine multiscopo Uso del tempo (TUS) 2022-2023
collection_period: 2022-2023 (per municipal notices in search results; Istat page did not state)
caveats: Istat microdata page: released file does not contain the diary data, which will be released separately. Diary results by time of day not yet found. Italy is covered only by HETUS 2010 (2008-09) in the meantime.

survey_name: Enquete Emploi du temps 2025-2026
collection_period: About 2025-10-13 to 2026-10-10 (six waves, September to September)
caveats: Collection not finished, so no results yet. Two diary days (weekday and weekend day). France is covered only by HETUS 2010 (2009-10).

survey_name: Encuesta de Empleo del Tiempo 2024/2025
collection_period: Full year from November 2024 (per search result, INE press page fetched showed only the 2009-10 edition)
caveats: Results reported by INE tender and technical project as due Q4 2026 (search results only). INE press page fetched describes the 2009-10 edition: 10-minute diary, main and secondary activities, more than 9,500 people. Spain covered by HETUS 2010 meanwhile.

publisher: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), National Statistics Office (NSO)
survey_name: Time Use Survey 2024 (report "Time Use in India, 2024", released 2025-03-28; fact sheet 2025-02-25)
edition_reference_period: TUS 2024 (second all-India TUS; first was Jan-Dec 2019)
activity_classification: ICATUS 2016 (3-digit "TUS activity classification"; div. 84 = Mass media use, 842 Watching/listening to television and video)
caveats: Diary is 24h recall 4:00 AM day before interview to 4:00 AM interview day, 48 slots x 30 min, CAPI interviewer-administered (not self-completed diary). Activities of >=10 min recorded, max 3 per slot; one is major and others minor; simultaneity asked. Report has NO time-of-day tables: only 4 charts (participation at time points across the day: employment 15-59, commuting 15-59, unpaid domestic/caregiving 6+, learning 6-14) with no tabulated values; no share asleep/leisure by hour. Slot-level microdata would allow derivation. Weekday/weekend not published as such: normal day vs other day (other day includes weekly off-days and holidays). Age bands published are 6-14, 15-29, 15-59, 60+ (not 5-year). Media use is ICATUS division 84 (841 reading, 842 watching/listening to TV and video, 843 radio/audio); no live-stream category. Estimates presented "considering all activities in slot" (equal time split) or major activity only. Access detail: report PDF); unit-level microdata at microdata.gov.in NADA catalogue DDI-IND-NSO-TUS-2024-24 (login/registration required.

survey_name: Comprehensive Modular Survey: Telecom (CMS:T) 2025, NSS Report No. 593
caveats: Stratified multi-stage household survey, 34,950 households / 142,065 persons, CAPI. Internet use = accessed internet at least once in last three months from any location, any device, any purpose. Only three age bands published (15-24, 15-29, 15+); no video, streaming or live-stream item (only "sent messages with attached files e.g. documents, pictures, video" skill item). Three-month fieldwork only. Access detail: report PDF); unit-level microdata at microdata.gov.in NADA catalog 239 (registration.

publisher: Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India (ORGI)
survey_name: Census of India 2011, Table C-17 Population by bilingualism and trilingualism (India, ID PC11_C17-00; downloaded DDW-C17-0000.XLSX)
edition_reference_period: Census 2011 (latest census; Census 2027 not yet published)
caveats: Self-reported languages: mother tongue, then 1st subsidiary language (= second language) and 2nd subsidiary language (= third language). NO proficiency scale, no age breakdown in C-17 (by mother tongue and sex only; all-area totals only). C-18 (bilingualism by age and sex) found in catalogue only for 2001, not 2011. 2011 is 15 years old. Downloaded with the emSign intermediate certificate added to the CA bundle because censusindia.gov.in serves an incomplete chain. Access detail: XLSX via NADA catalog.

publisher: National Population Commission (NPC) Nigeria with ICF (The DHS Program, USAID-funded)
survey_name: Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey 2024 (NDHS 2024)
caveats: Household survey, women 15-49 and men 15-59 only (not whole population). Internet use item is general (any purpose); no video/live-stream item; media exposure items cover TV/radio/newspaper. Literacy tested in a language on card, no English ability variable identified in indicator list (not checked in microdata). Access detail: DHS API / StatCompiler; microdata registration.

publisher: Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) with ICF (The DHS Program)
survey_name: 2022 National Demographic and Health Survey (NDHS 2022)
caveats: Women 15-49 only for internet-use indicator (men value not returned by API for PH2022DHS). General internet use, no video/live-stream item. Fetched from DHS API, not from PSA site (PSA blocked automated access). Access detail: DHS API / StatCompiler; microdata registration.

publisher: National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) Nigeria, with UN Women
survey_name: Nigeria Time Use Survey 2024 (NTUS 2024), first standalone TUS; report published 2025-05-01; microdata NGA-NBS-NTUS-2024-v1.0
collection_period: 2024-08-22 to 2025-03-10 (two seasonal rounds: dry and wet)
slot_length: 60 (hourly grid, 4:00-4:59 to 3:00-3:59; activity duration recorded in minutes per line)
caveats: NOT NATIONAL: representative only for four states (Borno, Cross River, Kaduna, Lagos); 3,600 households, 6,431 individuals aged 15+, two Kish-selected members per household. Diary 4:00am yesterday to 3:59am today, hourly grid with main activity and secondary activity columns, location and technology-use columns; interviewer-administered CAPI. Report itself states secondary (simultaneous) activity data "was not properly captured". No time-of-day tables in report (daily average minutes and participation only). Only mass media use (ICATUS) available, no video/live-stream split. Individual questionnaire has mobile phone ownership/internet access yes/no items and literacy in any language, no English ability. Fieldwork Aug 2024 - Mar 2025 spans both seasons (approx. 6.5 months). Access detail: report PDF); microdata via NBS microdata catalogue (registration/login required; confidentiality declaration.

survey_name: A Survey of Time Use, 2010 (Report 02-02-00; published 2013); microdata Version 1.2 via DataFirst catalog 497
edition_reference_period: TUS 2010 (second Stats SA TUS; first was 2000). No later Stats SA TUS found (the "TUS 2021" lead was not verified: searches and the ISIbalo TUS page listing show only 2000 and 2010)
collection_period: 2010-10 to 2010-12 (Q4 only, one quarter; last week of each month, alongside QLFS)
activity_classification: Stats SA activity classification based on UN trial ICATUS; 10 major categories incl. "Mass media use"
caveats: OLD: 2010, 15+ years. Only Oct-Dec collected (partial year, no seasonality). 39,897 respondents aged 10+; two persons per household selected via grid; diary 04h00 to 04h00, 30-minute slots, up to 3 activities per slot with simultaneity flag, two location codes. Report has NO time-of-day tables: only daily participation and mean minutes by sex, age group (10-17, 18-45, 46+), province, day of week (Table 3.7 participation by day of week for SNA and non-SNA production). Mass media use category includes TV, radio, other. Time-of-day derivation possible from DataFirst microdata. Stats SA website sits behind Incapsula bot protection; PDF was retrieved via WebFetch and read locally. Access detail: report PDF); microdata public use files at DataFirst (registration on DataFirst portal.

survey_name: General Household Survey 2025 (Statistical release P0318, published 2026-05-26)
caveats: Household-level internet access only (share of households with at least one member with access to or use of internet at any location; type of access). No individual internet use by age, no video/streaming item, no English item in the release (only home-language-like disability item). Retrieved as PDF through WebFetch because Stats SA sits behind Incapsula. Access detail: report PDF; microdata SAS/SPSS/STATA via ISIbalo/DataFirst.

survey_name: Census 2022: language most often spoken in the household (as analysed in Cultural Dynamics in South Africa, Report 03-01-84, Feb 2025)
caveats: Question is "Which language does (name) speak most often in this household?" = home language, NOT English ability or proficiency. Report gives national, provincial, metro and population-group shares; no age breakdown found. Census 2022 undercount noted by Stats SA. Access detail: report PDF; census 2022 tables on Stats SA.

publisher: Independent Communications Authority of South Africa (ICASA)
survey_name: The State of the ICT Sector Report of South Africa (31 March 2026)
caveats: Regulator supply-side statistics (subscriptions, revenue, coverage, licensed streaming platforms); relies on Stats SA GHS for household access; no individual-level live-stream, online-video or age-band usage measure found (searched text for internet users, streaming, age group, survey).

survey_name: General Household Survey 2025 (mid-decade; register-based population plus sample survey run within 2025 Comprehensive Labour Force & Household Survey); tables C020022 (language literate in) and C020029 (language most / second most frequently spoken at home) by age group
edition_reference_period: GHS 2025 (reference date 2025-06-30; published June 2026; tables updated 2026-06-30 / 2026-07-03); previous Census of Population 2020 Statistical Release 1
collection_period: 2025 (sample survey fieldwork during 2025 CLFHS; exact months not stated in fetched text)
caveats: Resident population (citizens + PRs), excludes non-residents (large foreign workforce). Literacy = ability to read in the language(s) (self-report), not spoken proficiency; no proficiency scale. Language most frequently spoken at home is a home-language measure; table excludes persons unable to speak and persons in one-person households and households of only unrelated persons. Values rounded to nearest 100; sample survey with sampling variability. Also Census of Population 2020 SR1 (fetched, older edition, superseded by GHS 2025; 2020 English at home 48.3% of residents 5+, literacy 15+ 97.1%). Access detail: SingStat Table Builder API; report PDF.

publisher: Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA); distributed via SingStat Table Builder and data.gov.sg
survey_name: Annual Survey on Infocomm Usage in Households and by Individuals: Individuals Internet Usage By Age Group (SingStat M920341) and Individuals Key Internet Activities (M920351)
edition_reference_period: Survey year 2024 (M920341, data last updated 2025-05-30); key internet activities to 2023 (M920351, updated 2024-08-23)
collection_period: annual survey; fieldwork months not stated in fetched tables
caveats: Sample design taken from a search excerpt only (about 3,500 households and 3,500 residents, face-to-face, two-stage stratified random sample of addresses from SingStat); IMDA survey report itself not fetched. Residents = citizens and PRs only. Age bands only 18-39, 40-59, 60+. No video/live-stream/streaming item; the closest published item is the "Leisure Activities" key internet activity (share of internet users), not by age and definition of "leisure activities" not seen in fetched metadata. Older IMDA series (2007-2018, 7-14, 15-24, 25-34, 35-49, 50+) exists at data.gov.sg d_5bdc3fbb49cfdf6d4ea7d826cc88bc84 but is superseded. Access detail: SingStat Table Builder API / data.gov.sg.

survey_name: Spring 2025 Global Attitudes Survey: internet use frequency (Q105), release 2025-09-08 (short read "Most adults across 24 countries are online at least several times a day")
caveats: Nationally representative face-to-face samples in India, Nigeria and South Africa (26,504 adults across 24 countries). Philippines and Singapore not surveyed in this wave. Age breakdown (under 35 vs 50+) only shown in charts of the short read, not in the topline text; topline gives country totals only. Internet-use frequency, no video or live-stream item in this release. Access detail: topline PDF and short read; dataset via Pew registration.

publisher: National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) Nigeria with World Bank LSMS
survey_name: Nigeria General Household Survey-Panel (Wave 5) 2023/2024, Survey Report
collection_period: post-planting visit Jul-Sep 2023 and post-harvest visit Jan-Mar 2024 (approx.; see report section on survey timing)
caveats: 4,715 households in 518 EAs; some EAs inaccessible due to conflict. ICT items limited to household mobile phone and internet access for individuals 10+. No time-use diary (no time-of-day data), no video/streaming item, no English item. Nigeria has not held a census since 2006. Access detail: report PDF); microdata at World Bank/NBS catalogues.

survey_name: National ICT Household Survey (NICTHS) 2024

Only search-engine snippets (not usable for figures) indicate ~44,000 households, individuals aged 10+. The 2019 edition individual questionnaire has internet activity items incl. leisure/lifestyle (gaming, music, streaming). Age breakdowns and any online video item unverified. caveats: NOT FETCHED: psa.gov.ph returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare). Search snippets only: covers mass media exposure and functional literacy; no evidence of an English-ability item. Functional literacy is in any language. Figures not recorded. Access detail: reported); automated access blocked.

caveats: Technical report: 7,533 interviews, quota sample of 2,084 face-to-face in 178 sampling points plus quota sample of 5,449 from online consumer panels; weighted to Census 2021 profiles.
